about: The code examples of the chapter 8 deck, in the order of the code slides (order = slide order). The page's chapter-code tab lists them by NAME in this order; every example is self-contained and runs with the Python standard library only; the expected result is what the run printed. The code is exactly the text of the deck's code boxes with the '>>> ' prompt removed; every statement is one line.

page_requirements: Python str, bytes, list, tuple, dict and the built-ins print, len, ord, chr, enumerate, zip, max, next (no import)

examples.name: Quotes and apostrophes
examples.code:
a = "Alice's cat"
b = 'Bob\'s cat'
print(a, len(a))
print(b, len(b))
print(type(b'a').__name__, type(r'a').__name__)
examples.expected:
Alice's cat 11
Bob's cat 9
bytes str

examples.name: Escape sequences

print(len('\\'), len('\''), len('\"'))

examples.name: Index into a string
examples.code:

print(greeting[0], greeting[4], greeting[-1])

examples.name: in, not in and immutability
concepts: The in and not in Operators
examples.code:

print(name[0:7] + 'the' + name[8:12])
print('Hello' in 'Hello, World', 'HELLO' in 'Hello, World')

examples.name: F-strings
examples.code:
name = 'Al'
age = 4000
print(f'My name is {name}. I am {age} years old.')
print(f'In ten years I will be {age + 10}. {{name}}')
examples.expected:
My name is Al. I am 4000 years old.
In ten years I will be 4010. {name}

examples.name: Older formatting styles
examples.code:

age = 4000

My name is Al. I am 4000 years old.
4000 years ago, Al was born.
Python unununium

examples.name: The book's rjust lines, re-run

examples.name: Alternating case program
examples.code:
flip = lambda i, c: c.lower() if i % 2 == 0 else c.upper()
print(''.join(flip(i, c) for i, c in enumerate('Hello, world!')))

examples.name: Pig Latin
examples.code:
cut = lambda w: next((i for i, c in enumerate(w) if c in 'aeiouy'), len(w))
pig = lambda w: w[cut(w):] + w[:cut(w)] + ('yay' if cut(w) == 0 else 'ay')
print(' '.join(pig(w) for w in 'my name is al'.split()))

examples.name: Table printer
examples.code:
a = ['apples', 'oranges', 'cherries', 'banana']
b = ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Carol', 'David']
c = ['dogs', 'cats', 'moose', 'goose']
table = [a, b, c]
w = [max(len(s) for s in col) for col in table]
print('\n'.join(' '.join(s.rjust(w[j]) for j, s in enumerate(r)) for r in zip(*table)))
examples.expected:
apples Alice  dogs
 oranges   Bob  cats
cherries Carol moose
  banana David goose

examples.name: Clipboard program, without the clipboard
concepts: Project 2: Add Bullets to Wiki Markup
examples.code:

lines = text.split('\n')
